sub_tasks.requirements: The centralized engine (control plane) and distributed runtime (execution plane) are implemented with RPC-based coordination and asynchronous P2P transfer between pipeline stages.
The centralized engine (control plane) is implemented as a single coordinator that separates scheduling logic from worker execution.
Code has been implemented that defines a centralized engine class/module which owns request queues, batch scheduling state, and holds handles/stubs to remote worker processes.

verification.spec: Import the centralized engine class and instantiate it with a mock config. Assert it exposes attributes/methods for request queues (e.g., waiting/running queues), a batch scheduler, and worker handles/stubs (list of RPC clients or Ray actor handles) with length equal to world_size.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the centralized engine performs a runtime initialization stage that delegates sub-models (per-stage layer partitions) to workers and triggers per-worker weight loading into device memory.

verification.spec: Instantiate the engine with world_size=2 pipeline-parallel and a small model (e.g., Llama2-13B or a stub). Call the initialization routine and assert each worker reports a distinct layer range covering the full model exactly once and that each worker's device memory usage after init is > 0 (weights loaded).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the centralized engine performs an execution scheduling stage that packs requests into batches based on memory capacity, request status, and profiling results before dispatching to workers.

verification.spec: Feed a synthetic request stream (varying prompt lengths) into the engine's scheduler with a fixed KV-cache capacity and profiling table. Assert that (a) scheduled batch size never exceeds capacity implied by requests' KV usage, (b) requests are dispatched to workers via the RPC interface, and (c) scheduling decisions depend on request status (waiting/running/finished).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that during the prefill phase the engine continuously packs prompts and sends them to the first-stage worker until the prefill-to-decode switching condition (from Approach-1) is triggered.

verification.spec: Instantiate the centralized engine with a stubbed switch predicate that returns False for the first K prefill dispatches then True. Feed a stream of prompts and assert that engine dispatches exactly K prefill batches to the first-stage worker before issuing any decode-mode command, and that all dispatches during that window carry the prefill phase indicator.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that during the decode phase the engine packs decode-step batches every iteration and removes completed requests from the active set at the end of each iteration.

verification.spec: Put the engine into decode mode with a batch of N requests where some are pre-marked completed (via a stubbed sampler emitting EOS). After each iteration, inspect the engine's active request set and assert that completed requests are removed before the next decode batch is packed, and that each iteration dispatches a decode-mode batch containing exactly the still-live requests.

sub_tasks.requirements: The distributed runtime (execution plane) is implemented as SPMD workers that execute per-stage computation without global scheduling state.
Code has been implemented that defines a worker/runtime class following an SPMD model, where each worker instance is bound to one GPU device and holds only its assigned model shard.

verification.spec: Import the worker/runtime module and assert (a) it defines a Worker class, (b) construction requires a device/rank argument and a layer-range or shard specification, (c) after init the worker holds only its assigned layers (check the module dict has fewer layers than the full model), and (d) two workers constructed with different ranks bind to different CUDA devices.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that initializes a global communication context on each worker holding world size, rank number, and peer rank identifiers used for point-to-point transfers.

verification.spec: Initialize the distributed runtime with world_size=4 across 4 processes. On each worker, assert that a global communication context object exists exposing world_size, rank, and peer-rank fields (prev_rank, next_rank or equivalent), and that these values are consistent across workers (rank i's next_rank == rank i+1's prev_rank).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each worker, upon receiving control information from the engine, resolves its stage position from the communication context and executes only the layers assigned to it.

verification.spec: Launch a 4-worker runtime holding a small model split into 4 stages. Send a control message from the engine describing a batch. Assert each worker executes only its assigned layer range (instrument forward with a per-worker call counter) and that the union of layers touched across ranks equals the full model with no overlap.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that a worker knows deterministically which peer rank to send activations to (next stage) and which peer rank to receive from (previous stage) based solely on its local communication context.

verification.spec: On each of 4 workers, without any engine input beyond the local communication context, query the worker for its send-destination and receive-source ranks. Assert rank i sends to i+1 and receives from i-1 (with endpoints handled per the runtime's convention) and that these values are computed solely from local context (mock/omit engine RPC and confirm the values are still available).

sub_tasks.requirements: RPC-based engine-to-worker coordination is implemented for metadata dispatch and lifecycle control.

Code has been implemented that establishes an RPC channel between the centralized engine and each distributed-runtime worker (e.g., via a Ray/torch.distributed.rpc/gRPC-style mechanism) usable to invoke remote methods on workers.

verification.spec: Start the centralized engine and 2 remote worker processes. From the engine, invoke a remote method (e.g., worker.ping() or worker.get_rank()) and assert it returns the expected value. Verify the RPC mechanism is one of {Ray, torch.distributed.rpc, gRPC} by inspecting imports.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the engine issues RPC calls transmitting only batch metadata (e.g., request IDs, token counts, batch composition, phase indicator) rather than full activation tensors.

verification.spec: Wrap the RPC transport with a spy that records the serialized payload size and type of every engine->worker call during a 100-request prefill+decode run. Assert that no payload contains tensors of activation shape [batch, seq, hidden]; all payloads contain only metadata fields such as request IDs, token counts, batch composition, and phase indicator.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for RPC-based lifecycle operations covering worker startup, model-shard loading, and shutdown, invoked from the centralized engine.

verification.spec: From the engine, call the RPC entrypoints for (a) worker startup / init_worker, (b) load_model_shard, and (c) shutdown, in sequence on 2 workers. Assert each call completes successfully, that after load_model_shard the worker reports non-empty GPU memory usage for its shard, and that after shutdown the RPC handles are closed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that RPC dispatch from the engine is non-blocking with respect to inter-stage activation transfers: the engine can enqueue the next batch without waiting for previously-dispatched batches to finish traversing the pipeline.

verification.spec: Inspect the centralized engine RPC dispatch code path: confirm that after issuing an RPC to a worker for batch N, the engine's scheduling loop can immediately construct/dispatch batch N+1 without joining on batch N's completion (e.g., the RPC returns a future/handle rather than blocking). Concretely, instrument the engine: dispatch 3 batches back-to-back on a 4-stage pipeline stub and measure that dispatch times of batches 2 and 3 begin before batch 1's completion callback fires.

sub_tasks.requirements: Asynchronous peer-to-peer activation transfer between pipeline stages is implemented.
Code has been implemented so that inter-stage activation communication uses NCCL point-to-point primitives (isend/irecv or equivalent) rather than collective all-reduce.

verification.spec: Grep the inter-stage communication code path for NCCL point-to-point primitives (torch.distributed.isend / irecv / send / recv or ncclSend/ncclRecv) and assert that no all_reduce / all_gather / reduce_scatter call is used for activation transfer between adjacent pipeline stages. A collective may only appear for tensor-parallel groups inside a stage, not between stages.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each P2P send/receive is issued asynchronously on a CUDA stream and workers can overlap communication of one micro-batch with computation of another.

verification.spec: In the worker P2P transfer code, confirm that torch.distributed.isend/irecv (or equivalent NCCL async ops) are used on a dedicated CUDA stream, NOT blocking send/recv. Run a 4-GPU pipeline test with two consecutive micro-batches and use torch.cuda.Event timing to verify that worker-k's compute for micro-batch i overlaps in time with its send of micro-batch i-1's activation.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that activation transfer between adjacent pipeline stages carries only the cut-layer hidden states (not KV cache or full model state) between the two neighboring ranks.

verification.spec: Instrument the P2P send call on each stage to record the tensor shape and destination rank. Run one forward pass across 4 stages. Assert that (a) each transfer's shape matches [tokens, hidden_size] (the cut-layer hidden state), (b) no KV cache tensors are transmitted between stages, and (c) each send goes to exactly rank+1 (the neighboring rank).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that each worker maintains a bounded queue of in-flight micro-batches, allowing multiple micro-batches to be simultaneously resident in the pipeline without stalling the engine's scheduling loop.

verification.spec: Configure the runtime with a small in-flight queue limit (e.g., 4). Feed the engine a rapid burst of 20 prefill batches. Assert that (a) at some point >=2 micro-batches are simultaneously resident on distinct stages (verified by timestamps of forward starts/ends per stage), and (b) the engine's scheduling loop continues to accept and enqueue new batches without blocking on prior batch completion.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that P2P transfers correctly synchronize with downstream compute (via stream events / wait) so that the next stage does not consume activations before the transfer completes, while still permitting the sender to proceed on other work.

verification.spec: Run 4-stage pipeline forward on a small model. Compare final logits/outputs against a single-GPU reference forward on the same inputs; assert numerical equivalence within fp16 tolerance (max abs diff < 1e-2). This validates that P2P transfers correctly synchronize before downstream compute. Additionally, instrument the sender to record whether it can enqueue the next batch's compute before its previous send is consumed by the receiver.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integration of the hierarchy controller with the temporally-disaggregated pipeline scheduling loop is implemented.

verification.spec: Inspect the batch scheduler class in the engine. verification.spec: Verify the repository's vllm dependency pins to 0.5.3 (check requirements/setup file). sub_tasks.requirements: During a sustained prefill-only workload on 4 GPUs, timeline traces show at least two micro-batches simultaneously in-flight across pipeline stages (i.e., stage k+1 computing batch b while stage k computes batch b+1), demonstrating that asynchronous P2P transfer overlaps with computation rather than serializing per-batch.

verification.spec: Run a sustained prefill-only workload (e.g., 500 prompts of length 512) on the 4-GPU pipeline with NCCL/CUDA event tracing enabled. verification.spec: Import the dataset-generation script. Run it on a small subset of ShareGPT V3 (with input length <1024 filter) against a small LLM stand-in. Verify output is a list/file of (prompt, output_length_in_tokens) pairs, that prompts have <1024 tokens, and output_length equals number of generated tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that splits the collected samples into 60% training, 20% validation, and 20% test sets for training the output length predictor.

verification.spec: Call the dataset-splitting function on a synthetic list of N samples. Assert that returned train/val/test lengths equal round(0.6N), round(0.2N), N-round(0.6N)-round(0.2N) respectively, and that the three splits are disjoint.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that trains a separate output length predictor per target model (Llama2-13B-chat, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, Llama2-70B-chat) using cross-entropy over the percentile bin labels.

verification.spec: Run the training script in a short-epoch mode on a small synthetic dataset for at least two target-model names. Verify that (a) a separate checkpoint file is produced per target model, (b) training loss is cross-entropy over percentile bin labels (inspect loss module), and (c) checkpoints load and produce class-probability outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The predictor's behavior on inputs and its integration into the inference pipeline are correct.
Code has been implemented that, given a raw prompt, tokenizes it for the BERT tokenizer, runs the predictor, and returns a single scalar predicted output length used by downstream scheduling.

verification.spec: Invoke the predict function with a raw prompt string. Verify (a) internal BERT tokenization is invoked, (b) function returns a scalar int/float predicted length (not a class index or distribution), and (c) predicted length is within the range of training-set output lengths.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that invokes the predictor for every incoming request before it is scheduled into the prefill phase, attaching the predicted length to the request metadata.

verification.spec: Instrument the request-admission path in the centralized engine. Submit N test requests and verify that for each request, the predictor is invoked exactly once before scheduling, and each request object carries a 'predicted_length' attribute prior to being placed into any prefill batch.

sub_tasks.requirements: The per-request classification accuracy of the trained predictor on the ShareGPT V3 test set is approximately 0.5214 for Llama2-13B-chat, 0.5805 for Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and 0.5234 for Llama2-70B-chat.

verification.spec: Train the output length predictor on 60% of ShareGPT V3 (filtered <1024 tokens) per model tokenizer, validate on 20%, and evaluate per-request top-1 classification accuracy on the remaining 20% test set for Llama2-13B-chat, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and Llama2-70B-chat. Expect ~0.52, ~0.58, and ~0.52 respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the accumulated prediction error over groups of N requests as the average absolute relative difference between the sum of predicted output lengths and the sum of actual output lengths, evaluated for group sizes N in {2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512}.

verification.spec: Run the accumulated-error evaluation script on the trained Llama2-13B predictor over the test set, grouping requests into size-256 buckets. Compute mean over buckets of |sum(pred)-sum(actual)|/sum(actual). Compare to reported 3.25% for 13B.

sub_tasks.requirements: The accumulated prediction error at group size 256 is approximately 3.25% for Llama2-13B-chat, 6.18% for Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, and 2.84% for Llama2-70B-chat.

verification.spec: Using the trained predictors and test split, group test samples into buckets of N=256 requests, and for each group compute accumulated relative error = |sum(predicted_lengths) - sum(actual_lengths)| / sum(actual_lengths), averaged over groups. Expect ~3.25% (13B), ~6.18% (32B), ~2.84% (70B).

sub_tasks.requirements: The total predictor execution overhead for 5,000 requests is approximately 1,418.861 ms on the L20 node and 833.695 ms on the A100 node, and contributes less than approximately 0.153% (L20) and 0.138% (A100) of total inference processing time.

verification.spec: Run the deployed predictor over 5000 ShareGPT V3 prompts on 4xL20 (batch through the BERT predictor in the same manner as during inference) and measure wall-clock time; expect ~1418.861 ms. Then divide by the shortest total run time from the throughput experiments (~929s L20) and confirm the ratio is <~0.2%.

sub_tasks.requirements: The AI-based greedy prefill approach interacts correctly with the rest of TD-Pipe's memory and phase-management logic.
Code has been implemented that uses the predicted output length (not the actual, unknown output length) when populating kvUsage, so that the switching decision is made purely from predictions.

verification.spec: Inspect UpdateUsage source code and verify getPredictLen(request) is called and used to update kvUsage; verify that no path reads the ground-truth output length (which would be unavailable at scheduling time). Also verify at runtime that requests carry predicted_length but not actual_length prior to completion.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that falls back to the recomputation strategy (freeing KV cache for recently arrived requests) when actual KV cache usage during the decode phase exceeds capacity due to prediction errors, without deadlocking the pipeline.

verification.spec: Set the predictor to intentionally underestimate output lengths so that actual KV usage will exceed capacity during decode. Run TD-Pipe on a synthetic workload and verify (a) the recomputation path is triggered (freeing KV for recently arrived requests), (b) the run completes all requests without deadlocking, and (c) no OOM error occurs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes a configurable manual KV cache occupancy ratio (e.g., 20%, 35%, 50%, 65%, 80%, 95%) as an alternative to the AI-based greedy prefill approach, so that ablation experiments can replace CheckSwitch with the fixed-ratio rule.

verification.spec: Import the TD-Pipe engine module and verify that a configurable KV-cache-occupancy-ratio switching rule can be enabled (e.g., via a config flag or constructor arg) that replaces the AI-based greedy prefill CheckSwitch. Instantiate the scheduler with ratios 0.20, 0.35, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80, 0.95 and assert that the switching predicate returns True exactly when current KV block occupancy >= ratio.

sub_tasks.requirements: The sliding-window based inter-batch work-stealing scheduler that rebalances decode batches at runtime is implemented, as described in Section 3.4 and Figure 9.
The initial partition of decode requests into batches equal to the number of pipeline stages/GPUs, each containing the same number of requests, is implemented.
Code has been implemented that, at the start of the decode phase, splits the collection of pending decode requests into N batches (where N equals the number of pipeline stages/GPUs) of equal size.

verification.spec: At the prefill->decode transition, inspect scheduler state. Verify the pending decode requests are partitioned into exactly N batches where N equals the pipeline stage count, and that the batch sizes differ by at most 1 (equal split when divisible).

sub_tasks.requirements: Given 512 requests and 4 pipeline stages, the initial partition produces 4 batches with batch sizes [128, 128, 128, 128], matching the initial condition in Figure 9.

verification.spec: Instantiate the scheduler with pipeline_stages=4 and 512 pending decode requests. Trigger initial decode partition and assert resulting batch sizes are exactly [128, 128, 128, 128].

sub_tasks.requirements: The sliding-window data structure that tracks recent batch sizes across the pipeline is implemented.
Code has been implemented for a sliding-window structure whose length is equal to the number of GPUs/pipeline stages and stores the most recent per-batch sizes needed to compute the running average.

verification.spec: Import the work-stealing scheduler. Instantiate with num_gpus=4. Verify a sliding-window attribute (e.g., deque) exists with maxlen == 4 that stores per-batch sizes. Push 5 batch sizes and verify only the last 4 remain.

sub_tasks.requirements: The sliding window is updated each time a batch completes and returns to the central scheduler, so that the window always reflects the last N batch sizes across pipeline stages.

verification.spec: Simulate a sequence of batch completions returning to the scheduler. After each completion, verify the sliding window contents equal the most recent N observed post-completion batch sizes, in insertion order.

sub_tasks.requirements: The per-iteration work-stealing scheduler logic that removes finished requests, computes the average, and decides how many requests to withhold or supplement is implemented.
When a batch returns from the pipeline, code removes the finished (completed) requests from that batch before further scheduling decisions are made.

verification.spec: Construct a batch of 128 requests with 48 marked as finished. Pass through the scheduler's batch-return handler. Verify the finished requests are removed before any average/stealing computation, leaving exactly 80 active requests in the batch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code computes the average batch size by subtracting the number of finished requests from the total requests tracked in the sliding window and dividing by the window length.

verification.spec: Unit test: instantiate the work-stealing scheduler with a sliding window of length N=4, push batch sizes [128,128,128,128], report 48 finished in batch 0, then invoke the average-computation function. Assert it returns (128*4 - 48)/4 = 116. Repeat with additional completions to verify formula avg = (sum(window) - finished_count) / window_length.

sub_tasks.requirements: If the current batch's remaining request count exceeds the computed average, the scheduler withholds the excess requests into a pending pool and submits only 'average'-many requests for execution.

verification.spec: Unit test: set computed average to 114 and pass a batch with 120 remaining requests. Call the scheduler's submit routine; assert exactly 114 requests are submitted for execution and 6 are placed in the withheld/pending pool accessible via the scheduler API.

sub_tasks.requirements: If the current batch's remaining request count is at or below the computed average, all remaining requests in that batch are resubmitted without withholding.

verification.spec: Unit test: set computed average to 116 and pass a batch with 80 remaining requests. Assert all 80 are submitted and the pending/withheld pool receives 0 new entries.

sub_tasks.requirements: In subsequent iterations, withheld requests from the pending pool are supplemented to under-full batches to bring them toward the current average batch size.

verification.spec: Unit test: pre-populate the withheld pool with 34 requests, then invoke the scheduler for a batch currently at size 80 with a target average of 114. Assert 34 requests are drained from the pool and merged into that batch, producing a submitted batch of size 114.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler uses batch size as the sole load-balance metric (rather than KV cache length or execution-time modelling), consistent with the paper's simplifying assumption.

verification.spec: Inspect the work-stealing scheduler source: verify the balance decision function's signature/inputs use only batch-size counts (integer number of requests per batch) and not KV cache lengths, per-request sequence lengths, or profiled execution times. Grep/AST-check that no per-request length fields are read inside the stealing decision path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Deterministic replay of the Figure 9 example produces the documented per-iteration behaviour of the work-stealing scheduler.

Running the scheduler on the Figure 9 scenario (batches starting at [128,128,128,128] with 48 requests finishing in batch 0 during iteration 1) produces a computed average of 116 after processing batch 0's completions, matching the paper's example.

verification.spec: Simulation test replicating Figure 9: initialize 4 batches at size 128 each, mark 48 completions in batch 0. Invoke the scheduler's average-computation after processing batch 0. Assert the returned average equals 116.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the Figure 9 example, after batch 0's 80 remaining requests are resubmitted (below the average 116, so 0 stolen) and batch 1 completes 8 requests, the recomputed average becomes 114 and the scheduler steals 6 requests from batch 1, submitting a batch of size 114.

verification.spec: Simulation test: continuing the Figure 9 example after batch 0 (80 resubmitted, 0 stolen), mark batch 1 as having 8 completions and 120 remaining. Invoke scheduler; assert the newly computed average is 114, 6 requests are stolen from batch 1, and the submitted batch size is 114.

sub_tasks.requirements: For batches 2 and 3 in the Figure 9 example (no completions in the first round), the scheduler steals 14 requests from each, submitting batches of size 114, matching the 'Steal' row values [0, -6, -14, -14] and 'bs (wi)' row [128, 114, 114, 114] in Figure 9.

verification.spec: Simulation test: continue Figure 9 scenario. For batches 2 and 3 (no completions, each with 128 remaining, average=114), invoke scheduler and assert 14 requests are stolen from each and both submitted at size 114. Verify the resulting 'Steal' sequence across the 4 batches is [0,-6,-14,-14] and 'bs(wi)' sequence is [80(resubmitted from batch0 iteration), 114, 114, 114] matching Figure 9.

sub_tasks.requirements: In the next iteration of the Figure 9 example, the 34 previously-withheld requests are supplemented into batch 0, producing a batch size of 114 (80 + 34) rather than leaving batch 0 at 80, so that all four batches converge to size 114.

verification.spec: Simulation test: after the first round of Figure 9 leaves 34 requests in the withheld pool, run the second-round scheduling of batch 0 (currently at 80). Assert all 34 withheld requests are moved into batch 0, submitted batch size = 114, and pool is emptied. Then verify batches 1-3 also converge to 114 in this iteration.

sub_tasks.requirements: The work-stealing approach is integrated with the temporally-disaggregated pipeline so that it operates during the decode phase only, and the load-balancing scheduling at the prefill-to-decode switching boundary remains independent from the dynamic stealing during decoding.

Code exposes a runtime switch (enable/disable flag) for the inter-batch work-stealing behaviour during the decode phase, allowing ablation runs with stealing disabled while keeping the initial equal-size partitioning at the prefill-to-decode boundary.

verification.spec: Verify a configuration flag (e.g. enable_work_stealing or --disable-work-stealing) exists in the engine's config/CLI. Run the engine twice on a small workload with the flag on and off; check via logs or a scheduler-state API that stealing/withholding is skipped in decode when disabled while the initial equal-size partitioning at the prefill->decode boundary still occurs (batch sizes equal at start of decode phase in both runs).

sub_tasks.requirements: The work-stealing scheduler is only invoked during decode-phase iterations (not during prefill), and it coexists with the centralized-engine batch scheduler without interfering with prefill scheduling.

verification.spec: Inspect scheduler code path: confirm the work-stealing routine is guarded to run only when the current phase state is DECODE. Add a test that puts the engine into PREFILL phase, invokes the scheduling loop, and asserts the withheld-pool/stealing routine is not called (e.g., via a mock/spy) and that prefill batching proceeds normally.

sub_tasks.requirements: The scheduler observes only one batch per iteration (as batches return sequentially from the pipeline stages) and correctly handles that other in-flight batches may complete additional requests before being observed, i.e., it does not require global synchronous observation.

verification.spec: Simulation test: mock a pipeline that returns batches one at a time in order. Between observations, mark additional completions on in-flight (unobserved) batches. Verify the scheduler updates the sliding window entry for each batch only when it returns, does not require global synchronization, and does not deadlock or crash when other batches have completions the scheduler has not yet observed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Iterative application of the scheduler on an imbalanced starting configuration causes per-batch sizes to converge toward the running average within a bounded number of iterations, demonstrating gradual rebalancing rather than one-shot balancing.

verification.spec: Simulation test: start with 4 batches of sizes [200, 50, 50, 50] and simulate random per-iteration completions (e.g., Bernoulli(p=0.05) per request) over 20 iterations with the scheduler active. Assert max(batch_sizes) - min(batch_sizes) decreases monotonically (allowing minor fluctuation) and converges to within a small delta (e.g. <= 5) of the mean within 20 iterations.

sub_tasks.requirements: Spatial intensity and temporal intensity metrics are computed via profiling, and the decode-to-prefill switch decision uses their comparison as described in Section 3.5 and Figure 10.
Profiling infrastructure that measures per-request decode execution time across batch sizes is implemented.
Code has been implemented to profile decode-step execution time for a range of decode batch sizes on the target model and hardware, storing results in a lookup table accessible to the scheduler.

verification.spec: Run the profiling script/entrypoint on the target model + hardware. Verify (a) it iterates over a range of decode batch sizes (e.g. 1..max), (b) writes a lookup table (JSON/pickle/csv) to a known path with entries mapping batch_size -> decode_step_time, and (c) the scheduler loads and queries this table at runtime (assert non-empty load and successful lookup for a mid-range batch size).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute, for each profiled batch size, the reciprocal of the average execution time per request (used as the per-batch-size intensity value).

verification.spec: Unit test: feed the profiling module a synthetic table of (batch_size, total_step_time). Assert the intensity value returned is 1/(total_step_time/batch_size) = batch_size/total_step_time for each entry, matching 'reciprocal of average execution time per request'.

sub_tasks.requirements: The profiler uses a sufficiently large decode batch size (representative of peak intensity operating regime) to establish the Peak reference value.

verification.spec: Inspect the profiler configuration: confirm it identifies a Peak intensity by using a batch size at least as large as a documented saturation threshold (e.g. >= 128 or the largest supported batch given memory). Verify that Peak is stored and later read by the SI computation. Run the profiler on a small config and check the recorded Peak batch size matches the configured saturation batch size.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that also profiles prefill execution time as a function of prefill batch/token count so that expected next-prefill duration can be estimated.

verification.spec: Run the prefill profiling routine on the target model. Assert it produces a table/function mapping (prefill token count or prefill batch shape) -> expected prefill execution time, saved to disk. Confirm the TI computation module loads and queries this table for pending prefills.

sub_tasks.requirements: Spatial intensity (SI) computation is implemented.

Code has been implemented that computes spatial intensity as SI = Achieved / Peak, where Achieved is the current decode batch's reciprocal-of-average-per-request time and Peak is the profiled peak value.

verification.spec: Unit test: mock the profile table so Peak=100 (reciprocal seconds per request) and set current decode Achieved=60. Call the SI function; assert it returns 0.6. Test additional cases (Achieved=100 -> SI=1.0, Achieved=25 -> SI=0.25).

sub_tasks.requirements: SI is recomputed each time the current decode batch size changes (e.g., after requests complete during the decode phase) so the switching decision uses the up-to-date value.

verification.spec: Integration test: simulate a decode loop where batch size drops from 128 -> 96 -> 64 due to completions. After each drop, invoke the switching-decision routine and record the SI value it used (via logging hook or a returned diagnostic). Assert SI is recomputed each iteration (different values for different batch sizes) rather than cached from the initial batch size.

sub_tasks.requirements: SI returns a value in [0, 1] and monotonically decreases as decode batch size drops below the peak-saturating batch size (verifiable via unit test with synthetic profile data).

verification.spec: Unit test with a synthetic profile where per-request time is monotonically non-increasing in batch size up to the peak-saturating batch size. Compute SI for batch sizes 1, 8, 32, 64, 128 (peak). Assert all SI values are in [0,1] and the sequence is monotonically non-decreasing (equivalently, SI decreases as batch size drops below peak).

sub_tasks.requirements: Temporal intensity (TI) computation is implemented as described in Section 3.5.

Code has been implemented that estimates the pipeline bubble duration at the current moment as the difference between the execution time of the longest pending prefill and the current decode step duration.

verification.spec: Unit test: mock pending prefill durations = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0] seconds and current decode step time = 0.5s. Invoke the bubble-estimation function; assert it returns 3.0 - 0.5 = 2.5s (longest pending prefill minus current decode step).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that estimates the total cycle time as the sum of all pending prefills' execution times, one decode step per batch, and the bubble.

verification.spec: Unit test: mock pending prefill durations = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0], number of decode batches = 4 with per-batch decode step = 0.5s, and bubble = 2.5s. Invoke total-cycle-time estimator; assert it returns sum(prefills) + num_batches*decode_step + bubble = 6 + 2 + 2.5 = 10.5s.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes temporal intensity as TI = 1 - Bubble / Total.

verification.spec: Unit test: with Bubble=2.5, Total=10.5, assert TI function returns 1 - 2.5/10.5 ≈ 0.7619. Test additional cases (Bubble=0 -> TI=1.0, Bubble=Total -> TI=0.0).

sub_tasks.requirements: The set of pending prefills used for TI computation is drawn from the request manager's ToDo queue (requests not yet prefilled), so TI reflects the actual next-cycle workload.

verification.spec: Inspect the TI computation code: confirm it enumerates pending prefills by querying the request manager's ToDo/pending-prefill queue (not e.g. all arrived requests or already-prefilled ones). Add a test that puts N requests into the ToDo queue, marks some as already prefilled, and asserts TI's prefill list length equals the number still pending (unfilled).

sub_tasks.requirements: TI returns a value in [0, 1] and decreases when there are more/longer pending prefills relative to the current decode step (verifiable via unit test with controlled prefill queue).

verification.spec: Unit test with controlled ToDo queues: (a) queue with 1 short prefill vs (b) queue with 5 long prefills, holding current decode step constant. Compute TI for both. Assert both TI values are in [0,1] and TI(b) < TI(a) (more/longer pending prefills yield smaller TI relative to current decode step).

sub_tasks.requirements: Decode-to-prefill switch decision policy based on SI vs TI comparison is implemented.
Code has been implemented so that at each decode step boundary the scheduler evaluates SI and TI and triggers a switch to the prefill phase when SI < TI, otherwise continues decoding.

verification.spec: Instantiate the scheduler with a mocked SI/TI provider. Feed sequences of (SI, TI) values at decode-step boundaries and assert the scheduler triggers a phase switch to prefill iff SI < TI, and continues decode otherwise. Verify the switch API is called exactly once per crossing.

sub_tasks.requirements: The switch decision runs only when there are pending prefills in the ToDo queue; if no prefills are pending, the system stays in decode until the queue is repopulated.

verification.spec: Set SI < TI (switch condition) but empty the pending-prefill ToDo queue. Step the scheduler and assert no switch occurs and decode continues. Then repopulate the queue and assert the switch fires on the next evaluation.

sub_tasks.requirements: On triggering a switch, the scheduler transitions control to the prefill batching path (matching the hierarchy-controller engine's phase-switch protocol) and stops issuing decode batches.

verification.spec: Drive the scheduler to a switch decision and instrument its output stream. Assert that after the switch signal, no further decode batches are dispatched and the next dispatched batch is a prefill batch produced by the prefill batching path.

sub_tasks.requirements: Integration and behavioral validation of the intensity comparison mechanism.
The intensity comparison module is wired into the centralized engine's scheduling loop such that switch decisions occur without stalling ongoing pipeline execution.

verification.spec: Run the centralized engine's scheduling loop with mocked workers that record dispatch timestamps. Trigger a switch decision mid-run and assert that in-flight pipeline micro-batches continue to execute (no barrier/stall observed) while the switch is scheduled to take effect at the next batch boundary.

sub_tasks.requirements: The profiling table, SI computation, and TI computation share consistent units (time per token or per request) so that SI and TI are numerically comparable on the same scale.

verification.spec: Inspect the SI and TI computation functions: assert Peak, Achieved (used in SI) and bubble, total (used in TI) are all derived from per-request time or per-token time in the same unit (e.g., seconds). Run a numerical sanity check where a hand-computed scenario yields SI and TI in [0,1] with expected ordering.

sub_tasks.requirements: The system logs SI, TI, current decode batch size, and pending-prefill count at each decision point to enable inspection of switching behavior over a full run.

verification.spec: Run a short end-to-end inference with logging enabled. Parse the log file and assert that each decision point emits a record containing SI, TI, current decode batch size, and pending-prefill count. Verify at least one record exists per decode iteration over a 100-step window.

sub_tasks.requirements: TP+SB, TP+HB, PP+SB, and PP+HB baselines are set up in vLLM v0.5.3 with the recomputation strategy, matching the paper's baseline definitions in Section 4.1.
The four baseline configurations are correctly instantiated on top of vLLM v0.5.3.
Code has been implemented to launch baselines using vLLM v0.5.3 as the underlying inference engine, with a version pin or check that fails if a different vLLM version is detected.

verification.spec: Import vllm and assert vllm.__version__ == '0.5.3'. Verify the baseline launcher module contains an explicit version check that raises on mismatch.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes a unified baseline launcher/entry point accepting a baseline identifier in {TP+SB, TP+HB, PP+SB, PP+HB} and configuring vLLM accordingly.

verification.spec: Invoke the launcher CLI/API with each of the four baseline IDs ('TP+SB', 'TP+HB', 'PP+SB', 'PP+HB'). Assert each invocation instantiates vLLM with the expected (tensor_parallel_size, pipeline_parallel_size, enable_chunked_prefill) tuple as documented, and rejects unknown IDs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to configure baselines to use 1, 2, and 4 GPUs (matching the sweep in Section 4.2) via appropriate parallelism-size arguments passed to vLLM.

verification.spec: For each baseline ID, invoke the launcher with num_gpus in {1, 2, 4} and inspect the resulting vLLM engine args. Assert the effective parallelism-size argument (tensor_parallel_size for TP-*, pipeline_parallel_size for PP-*) equals the requested num_gpus.

sub_tasks.requirements: TP+SB (tensor parallel + separate batching) baseline is set up as the default vLLM configuration.
Code has been implemented that instantiates vLLM with tensor_parallel_size equal to the number of GPUs and pipeline_parallel_size = 1 for the TP+SB baseline.

verification.spec: Invoke launcher for TP+SB with N GPUs and capture the LLM/AsyncLLMEngine constructor kwargs. Assert tensor_parallel_size == N and pipeline_parallel_size == 1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented ensuring that TP+SB disables chunked prefill (enable_chunked_prefill=False) so that prefill and decode requests are batched separately rather than in hybrid batches.

verification.spec: Capture the vLLM engine kwargs when the launcher is invoked for TP+SB and assert enable_chunked_prefill is False (or the equivalent scheduler policy disables chunked prefill).

sub_tasks.requirements: Runtime behavior verified: for TP+SB, each transformer layer issues two all-reduce collectives across the tensor-parallel group (consistent with the paper's description in Section 4.1).

verification.spec: Launch TP+SB with 2 GPUs on a small model, patch torch.distributed.all_reduce (or the NCCL wrapper) to count invocations per layer over one forward pass, and assert the count per transformer layer equals 2.

sub_tasks.requirements: TP+HB (tensor parallel + hybrid batching with chunked prefill) baseline is correctly configured.
Code has been implemented that instantiates vLLM with tensor_parallel_size equal to the number of GPUs, pipeline_parallel_size = 1, and enable_chunked_prefill=True for TP+HB.

verification.spec: Capture vLLM engine kwargs when the launcher is invoked for TP+HB with N GPUs and assert tensor_parallel_size == N, pipeline_parallel_size == 1, enable_chunked_prefill == True.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sets a chunked-prefill chunk size / max_num_batched_tokens for TP+HB, and the same chunk-size setting is applied consistently across all TP+HB runs.

verification.spec: Invoke launcher for TP+HB across all GPU counts and models used in Section 4.2. Assert max_num_batched_tokens (or the chunk-size argument) is set to the same value in every run and matches the value declared in the launcher config.

sub_tasks.requirements: Runtime behavior verified: TP+HB batches contain a mix of prefill chunks and decode tokens (hybrid batches) as opposed to purely-prefill or purely-decode batches.

verification.spec: Run TP+HB on a small model with a mix of new prompts and in-flight decode requests. Instrument vLLM's scheduler to log per-batch composition. Assert at least one batch contains both prefill tokens (chunked) and decode tokens simultaneously.

sub_tasks.requirements: PP+SB (pipeline parallel + separate batching) baseline is correctly configured.
Code has been implemented that instantiates vLLM with pipeline_parallel_size equal to the number of GPUs, tensor_parallel_size = 1, and enable_chunked_prefill=False for PP+SB.

verification.spec: Capture vLLM engine kwargs when the launcher is invoked for PP+SB with N GPUs and assert pipeline_parallel_size == N, tensor_parallel_size == 1, enable_chunked_prefill == False.

sub_tasks.requirements: Runtime behavior verified: PP+SB uses only point-to-point send/recv between pipeline stages (no all-reduce within a layer) and never mixes prefill and decode tokens inside the same micro-batch.

verification.spec: Run PP+SB with 2 GPUs on a small model. Patch torch.distributed collective ops to count all_reduce and send/recv invocations for one forward pass. Assert all_reduce count == 0 within transformer layers and send/recv > 0 at stage boundaries. Also instrument the scheduler to assert every dispatched batch is either pure-prefill or pure-decode (never mixed).

sub_tasks.requirements: PP+HB (pipeline parallel + hybrid batching with chunked prefill) baseline is correctly configured.
Code has been implemented that instantiates vLLM with pipeline_parallel_size equal to the number of GPUs, tensor_parallel_size = 1, and enable_chunked_prefill=True for PP+HB.

verification.spec: Capture vLLM engine kwargs when the launcher is invoked for PP+HB with N GPUs and assert pipeline_parallel_size == N, tensor_parallel_size == 1, enable_chunked_prefill == True.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that PP+HB uses the same chunked-prefill chunk-size setting as TP+HB, ensuring a fair comparison between the two hybrid-batching baselines.

verification.spec: Invoke launcher for both TP+HB and PP+HB with matched (model, num_gpus) settings. Extract the chunk-size argument (max_num_batched_tokens or equivalent) from each and assert they are equal.
